SLAM has a long history in computer vision, traditionally relying on feature-based methods (e.g., ORB-SLAM) or direct methods (e.g., DSO, LSD-SLAM).

The advent of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) [Mildenhall et al. 2020] introduced implicit neural representations for novel view synthesis, leading to "Neural SLAM" methods that optimize neural fields jointly with camera poses.

More recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting [Kerbl et al. 2023] has been adapted for SLAM (e.g., SplaTAM, Gaussian Splatting SLAM) due to its fast rendering speed and explicit representation, offering a balance between the quality of NeRF and the efficiency of traditional point-based methods.
Hybrid approaches combining neural fields and Gaussians (e.g., PIN-SLAM, CP-SLAM) are also emerging to leverage the strengths of both representations.
